name: Mind and Body
_what: Info film for the Mind and Body domain: its five peoples (Cogitants, Somatics, Syllogists, Figurists, Masons of the Give), their homes, costs, heretics or pure poles, one figure each, and the two cross-axis arguments. Every string in lines, after, name and title is player-facing.

lines: Mind and body: five peoples.
Three belong to Mind, the only domain with three sects and three sources of power.
The Cogitarium.
Pale halls float above open ground. Beneath them, nothing.
Cogitants train memory, focus and reason until thought acts on the world.
Sharp, not wise. They are clear about the difference.
after: Their heretics, the Openers, read minds that never opened.

lines: They have nearly left their bodies behind, and they are dying of it.
Custodians keep the bodies, bed after bed, for a fee.
Sesh of the Quiet Blow ends fights with a thought. She reads the decision, not the body.
after: She would like to be surprised, once.

lines: The High Temple of the Body climbs a mountain in terraces.
Every soul on it trains breath, poise and endurance, as devotion.
Somatics train the body until it answers the will completely: breath, heartbeat, pain, fear.
Control, past where control should end.
Thought neglected, the Temple is forgetting how to warn itself.
It looks down at the Cogitarium with a grief it rarely says aloud.
When one person must stop a fight, the Temple sends Marn of Two Forms.
His first form ends fights without ending people.
Soma works the will through the body, Noesis through the mind.
Both are the same refusal of an ordinary ceiling.
Between them, the Middle Way trains body and mind under one roof.
Both poles call it a compromise. It calls them cautionary tales.
The Axiom is a city built like an argument, from premises, in order.
Its people drop any position the moment it is shown false.
Syllogists build arguments that compel the reasonable. The craft proves only what is true, and fails against anyone who simply refuses.
after: To be irrefutably right is a lonely country.

lines: In the Proof-Halls every argument they ever made is kept, its errors signed by the people who made them.
At their pure pole, the Bloodless Hold: reason purified of feeling, which turns out to be something with reason's face.
Quillon Vey wrote himself into a proof, and cannot die while it stands.
Those who try to refute it and fail, he kills.
Cloudform resists being mapped.
Its streets change width as you look along them.
Figurists draw marks that do in the world what they mean.
Draw the figure truly, and the world briefly consents to match it.
after: The Shapers hold a person to a figure they cannot step out of.

lines: At the Figure-Works the meanings do exactly what they mean.
Not always what was wanted: the whole history of their disasters.
Seren, Who Is Not Looked At, lives veiled among statues of those she loved.
She wants to meet someone's eyes and have them still be there.
Bedrock. Dressed stone in deep courses, cranes at every corner.
The Masons build things that outlast the arguments about them.
To the Masons of the Give, the real is what you can touch, weigh and set.
Everything else is a claim awaiting proof.
after: The Levellers take a person's meaning apart in front of them.

lines: The Weighing Yard has never been wrong about a material.
It has been catastrophically wrong about several things that were not.
In the Leaden Deep, where no prayer lands, Asterion keeps the Masons' maze.
He has never seen the sky. He asks every visitor to describe it.
Mason and Figurist are one argument, centuries old. Where a Mason stands, a figure fails.
after: Neither has won, and both are correct.

lines: Every Reach is leaning harder into its own extreme.
The Cogitarium abandons more bodies.
At the Held Yard, one side stops the fight. The other works out why it started.
after: Neither has convinced the other that its half is harder.
